title: Natural projection to the two-term naive cotangent truncation
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective $A$-algebra map, where $P$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra on any set of variables or a localization of such an algebra. Put $J=\ker(P\to B)$ and $C(P)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $\mathrm d([h])=\mathrm dh\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a canonical map $L_{B/A}\to C(P)$ inducing an isomorphism $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{B/A}\simeq C(P)$. Truncation means replacing degree $-1$ by the cokernel of the incoming differential and discarding degrees below $-1$. This comparison is natural under commutative diagrams of such surjective presentations: a compatible map $P\to P'$ over $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$ gives the semilinear chain map $C(P)\to C(P')$, with $[h]\mapsto[h']$ in degree $-1$ and $\mathrm dp\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm dp'\otimes b'$ in degree $0$, and it commutes in the derived category with the standard functoriality map on $L$. No vanishing below degree $-1$ and no finite generation of the differential module is asserted.
